newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Pros trade ODP, Staples unwound.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Pros trade ODP, Staples unwound.

text.p: Professionals were the main traders in Office Depot Inc options and were focusing on the puts, while investors were mostly unwinding positions in Staples Inc options, traders said Friday.
The heavy activity in both sets of options came as the U.S. Federal Trade Commission voted 4-1 against a revamped merger between the two office superstores.

After an intraday halt, Office Depot shares were down six points at 13 on consolidated volume of more than 19 million shares by 1330 CST/1930 GMT. Staples added 3/4 to 22. Turnover there was nearly 15 million shares.
"I've never seen such a large concentration of professional orders," Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said of Office Depot options trading.
"The bulk of the activity is in the puts, not the calls," he said. "I think it's a lot of professionals that were protecting themselves, more so than speculation out there."
But Schwarz added that he expected speculation to increase once Friday's news was digested.
Matthew Schaffer, the specialist in Staples options for TFM Investment Group, said the Staples options activity indicated some investors still expected a deal to go through.
The FTC said an Office Depot-Staples merger would lead to higher office supply prices for consumers.
Staples said it was evaluating whether to fight the FTC decision in court.
"Basically what we're seeing here is a lot of people are unwinding and trying to take off positions," Schaffer said. "They don't want the risk anymore.
"But a small percentage still has some optimism this thing is going to go through and they are trying to roll out their positions to farther out months," he said.
The most active Staples options were the April 30 put, which traded nearly 4,000 contracts, and the April 20 call, which traded roughly 3,270.
The May 22-1/2 call traded about 1,650 contracts and the May 30 put traded 2,285.
Schwarz noted that the bulk of the Office Depot options trading was in the April series "because this is a short-term event."
The Office Depot April 15 put traded more than 16,500 contracts and the April 20 call traded about 11,900, making them the two most active.

The April 15 call traded 8,100 contracts and the April 17-1/2 put traded nearly 5,500, rounding out the most active Office Depot options. Outside of the April series, the May 15 call traded about 4,570 contracts.
Volatilities in both Office Depot and Staples options fell sharply, traders said.

"What I think is really interesting is that it's an extremely professional crowd" trading Office Depot options, Schwarz said. "All the broker dealers, the arbitrageurs and the professional trading desks are using options as a strategy to limit risk and to maximize profit."
